solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pistol to flourish, pursuing something sparking in tree

parts.note: wit is a sparkling, quick intelligence
gat is slang for a gun
to boom is to thrive or prosper

explanation.surface: A gunfight scene: someone brandishes a pistol after a spark flares up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuing' puts the pistol and the flourish after the wit, so the pieces read in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The witgatboom is a South African shepherd's tree, its Afrikaans name meaning white-hole tree.

clue.text: Raised hatch, mainly to view storms across loch?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read from the bottom upwards
mainly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to hatch or produce young, as fish do

explanation.surface: Someone climbs up through a raised hatch to watch storms sweep over a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAWN loses its last letter to SPAW, which turns upwards to WAPS. The question mark and 'across loch' flag a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wap is a Scots and northern dialect word for a sudden blow or a squall of stormy weather.

clue.text: Mongolian ready to pull personnel on Karakoram peak up

parts.note: to tug is to pull
human resources, the personnel department

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means this name is written bottom to top

parts.note: K1, also called Masherbrum, is a Karakoram mountain; the 1 serves as I

explanation.surface: A climber is ready to haul staff up a Himalayan summit in Mongolia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not an adjective here but slang for cash. Karakoram peaks are numbered K1, K2 and so on; the 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The tughrik is the monetary unit of Mongolia, and the ready is an old slang term for cash money.

clue.text: Expensive medicine, a superior leftover, turned to a bitter fluid

parts.note: taken as written
U means upper class, superior
a rump is a remnant left over

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the little word before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the second a in the clue, taken as written
bile is the bitter digestive juice

explanation.surface: A pricey remedy, the posh dregs of something, has soured into a bitter liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurum potabile, Latin for drinkable gold, was a costly alchemical cordial of dissolved gold taken as a cure-all.

clue.text: Italian composer's lack of reserve upset yours truly

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned over, so the phrase is read bottom to top

parts.note: no sub: no substitute on the bench
yours truly means the speaker, I

explanation.surface: A composer's lack of restraint has offended the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack of reserve' reads as a want of restraint, but it means no reserve player: NO SUB, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferruccio Busoni was an Italian composer and virtuoso pianist, famous for his Bach transcriptions.

clue.text: Played with brass ring on mop head in need of replacement

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: letters in need of replacement are to be put back in different places

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cleaner notices a ring on a mop whose head is worn out and needs replacing.
explanation.definitionFit: To oompah is to play the deep, rhythmic bass notes of a brass band, as a tuba does.

clue.text: School do printed material, omitting biblical books

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so some letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: chintz is a printed cotton fabric
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A school event is printed in a programme that leaves out the scripture readings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party but means a swindle. CHINTZ minus NT leaves CHIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiz is schoolboy slang, made famous by the Molesworth books, for a swindle or cheat.

clue.text: Idiot replacing line from Yank's long mail

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes the place of another within the word

parts.note: to yank is to haul
L is the abbreviation for line
berk is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A fool has taken a line out of an American's lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' and 'mail' suggest an American's post; BERK takes the place of the L in HAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A hauberk is a long coat of chain armour reaching to the knees, worn by medieval knights.

clue.text: Unknown to babble at length about one tiny item charged

parts.note: an algebraic unknown, x, y or z

indicators.note: about means going round, so the babbling phrase surrounds the number

parts.note: to witter on is to chatter at tedious length
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone talks on and on about a tiny thing they have been billed for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' hints at a bill, but it is electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A zwitterion is a molecule carrying both a positive and a negative electrical charge, such as an amino acid.

clue.text: Antelopes recorded originally in Pliny's case with jokes

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so only the two end letters of the name are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of Pliny

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter sits within the rest

parts.note: gags are jokes

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so just the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of recorded

explanation.surface: Antelopes were first written up in Pliny's natural history, along with some jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pliny the Elder did write about the pygarg in his Natural History, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pygarg is an antelope named in the Bible and by classical writers, thought to be a kind of addax.

clue.text: Eastern ceremony with complicated mass Irish-American brought west

parts.note: a mat is a tangled mass, as of hair

indicators.note: in an across clue, moving west means going right to left, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: IR is an abbreviation for Irish
US stands for American

explanation.surface: An Irish-American brings an elaborate Mass to the West as an oriental rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' sounds religious, beside 'ceremony', but means a tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A matsuri is a Japanese festival, often a Shinto shrine celebration with processions and portable shrines.

clue.text: Admiration for wonder article in truth a lot may put differently

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter goes into the following words
something put differently is expressed in another arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of these four words
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay suggests that genuine admiration for wonders could be phrased in many ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Thaumatolatry, from Greek thauma, a marvel, plus -latry, worship, is the excessive veneration of miracles.

clue.text: Bitter blow for Italy: cheers welcoming Spaniard getting bronze

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the thanks word surrounds the following pieces

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
Ramón is a typical Spanish man's name
a bronze is a tan

explanation.surface: Italy suffers a bitter blow in sport even as the crowd cheers a Spaniard taking bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter blow' reads as a setback, but it is a cold wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The tramontana is a cold, dry north wind blowing down from the mountains over Italy and the Adriatic.

clue.text: Once again alien force invades

indicators.note: something that invades gets inside, so this letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: ET, the film's extraterrestrial
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: An alien army invades a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic sense: the word is a newt today but meant again long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Eft is an obsolete English adverb meaning afterwards or a second time, from Old English.

clue.text: Triple crown for Scotland finally and rugby clubs clan briefly over the moon

indicators.note: over here means spread across, so the shortened word straddles the moon
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter
the crown is the top, and in a down clue the top letter is the first

parts.note: the first letter of Scotland

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of and
RU is rugby union
C is clubs in card notation
taken as written before shortening
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Scotland wins rugby's Triple Crown and the whole clan is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Triple Crown is won by beating the other three home nations in rugby, but 'crown' is just a top letter. CLAN cut to CLA straddles IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sdrucciola is an Italian term for a triple, or dactylic, rhyme, stressed on the third syllable from the end.

clue.text: On reflection, quietly approve sort of leather wader

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
to OK is to approve
kid is leather made from young goatskin

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, someone quietly approves a particular leather boot for wading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leather wader' looks like a wading boot; the wader is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dikkop is the South African stone curlew, a long-legged bird of the wading kind with large eyes.

clue.text: College cleaner embarked on a trip

indicators.note: a trip can mean a stumble, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A university cleaner has set off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a trip' reads naturally after embarked, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge and Oxford colleges a bedmaker is the domestic servant who tidies students' rooms.

clue.text: You and one drunk to set about irrational perfectionist

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the drink word surrounds the number that follows

parts.note: a toast is the person or thing that is drunk to
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: You and a drunken companion begin to set about an unreasonable perfectionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like a sot or an anagram signal, but 'one drunk to' is the object of a toast. 'Irrational' is the number, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopiast is a believer in utopias, someone dreaming of an ideal flawless society, hence a perfectionist.

clue.text: Asphalt that's unlimited suited for covering nearly half of internal area

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the shortened outfit word surrounds the rest
without limits means losing the boundaries, so the first and last letters go
half of the word, then nearly that, leaves only its opening three letters

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written before trimming
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A tarmac that is endlessly suitable for surfacing most of an indoor space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly half' is a two-stage cut: halve the eight-letter word, then drop one more letter. 'Unlimited' strips both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Uintaite, or gilsonite, is a natural black asphalt mined in the Uinta Basin of Utah.

clue.text: Grey matter involving the writer's one vexatious to Scottish lawyer

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so the brains word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: nous is common sense, brains
the writer is I, so the writer's is I'm
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer finds a brainy writer tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimious is a Scots legal term for excessive or unduly burdensome, from Latin nimius, too much.

clue.text: English misses lacking in variety fell for Wexford wastrel

indicators.note: misses means goes without, so a letter is left out of the next word

parts.note: stale means tired and repetitive
E is the abbreviation for English
to fell an opponent is to knock out, KO

explanation.surface: Young women from England with dull lives fall for a ne'er-do-well in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English misses' looks like English girls; it means E goes missing from STALE. Wexford is a county in south-east Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalko is Irish slang for an idle, shabby-genteel man without means or occupation, a good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Snake's tongue half concealed: I see it now!

indicators.note: with half concealed, only one half of the word is visible, so the back half goes

parts.note: a tongue is a language
aha is the cry of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: A snake's forked tongue is half hidden, until someone spots it and cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' suits a snake but means a language; its first half is LANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The langaha is a Madagascan tree snake whose snout ends in a long leaf-shaped appendage.

clue.text: Hold centrists in Congress to ban, advancing nothing

indicators.note: nothing is the round letter, and advancing it means moving it from the back of the word to the front
the centrists are those in the middle, so only the central letters of the word are used

parts.note: the two central letters of Congress
to veto is to forbid

explanation.surface: Moderates in Congress block a ban, getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' names the O, the last letter of VETO, which moves to the front to make OVET.
explanation.definitionFit: A grovet is a wrestling grip in which one arm goes over an opponent's shoulder and round the neck.

clue.text: Eastenders in dramatic row slam Corrie

indicators.note: those at the east end, in an across reading the right-hand end, are the final letters

parts.note: the last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: In a dramatic EastEnders row, a character slams Coronation Street.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders and Corrie (Coronation Street) are British TV soaps, but Eastenders here means end letters and a corrie is a mountain hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cwm is the Welsh word and corrie the Scottish word for a steep bowl-shaped valley at a mountain head.

clue.text: Awful pun: pilgrim is colouring deeply?

indicators.note: awful means dreadfully done, so the following letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A terrible pun makes a pilgrim blush crimson.
explanation.definitionFit: To impurple is to tinge with purple; the question mark admits the stretch from purple to deep colour generally.

clue.text: Bar turned around by cracking beer

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it, so this letter goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
x is the times sign, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A pub is turned upside down by someone opening a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned around' looks like a reversal signal but belongs to the definition: the bar round which a wheel turns.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or spindle on which a wheel rotates.

clue.text: Float old things the competent should know about primarily

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
someone competent knows the ropes

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter alone is taken

parts.note: the first letter of about

explanation.surface: A seasoned hand ought to know all about an old float.
explanation.walkthrough: To know the ropes, an old sailing idiom, is to understand how things work.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oropesa is a torpedo-shaped float towed in minesweeping to hold the sweep wire out at depth.

clue.text: Recalled Egypt once, note, appearing in fifteen stained glass pieces?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the following pair is read backwards
appearing in means being inside, so the reversed pair sits within the number

parts.note: XV is fifteen in Roman numerals
the United Arab Republic, Egypt's name from 1958 to 1971
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Memories of ancient Egypt surface in fifteen panes of a stained glass window.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitraux is French for stained-glass windows, the plural of vitrail; the question mark flags the borrowing.

clue.text: Cold, salty water for winding back ligature

indicators.note: winding back means turning backwards, so the run of letters is read the other way

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the sea is salt water

explanation.surface: Cold brine is used to wind back a binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ligature' suggests a surgical tie; it is the joined letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesc is the Old English name of the rune and letter for the joined ae vowel.

clue.text: Exchanging tips on craft, starship's engineer to accept bread snack?

indicators.note: the tips of the word craft are its two end letters, and exchanging means they swap places with each other

parts.note: Scotty is the Starship Enterprise's engineer in Star Trek
to take is to accept

explanation.surface: On a spacecraft, the ship's engineer swaps ends with someone while agreeing to a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTTY TAKE swaps its C and T, the ends of craft, to read STOTTY CAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stottie cake is a flat, round loaf from north-east England, split and filled as a sandwich.
